summary:
[  edit  ]
The Multi Touch In  DAT  is used for receiving messages and events from the Windows standard multi-touch API. It captures all the messages, where each new message changes the table it outputs. When a messages is added to the  DAT , any script can be called pointing to the new message. The Multi Touch In  DAT  can be sent to the  Render Pick DAT , or used with interactTouch methods in the  Panel Component  and  Web Render TOP .  Multi Touch  DAT  is not supported on macOS.
It can output either of two table formats: (1) Raw Events as a FIFO (first in - first out) list, or (2) ID Table, which is the events processed into a more usable one-row-per-finger table.
The Raw Events format creates a FIFO-type  DAT  (see also  FIFO DAT ) which, for each multi-touch event, has a row added to the bottom of the table while at the same time a row at the top is deleted.
Note: To operate panel gadgets with multi-touch screens that send events through the Windows event stream, multi-touch works without requiring DATs. You need to use the  DAT  when using multiple fingers on one panel, like in a container displaying a 3D render whose objects you want to pick.
The ID table format includes the columns:
id  - every finger press increases the id by 1
sn  - an ongoing count of each finger press.
select  - when 1, this row represents a finger is down.
downf  - the absolute frame number when the finger press occurred.
upf  - the absolute frame number that the finger press ended
x ,  y  - the position, in pixels in the horizontal and vertical directions.  NOTE : The  x  and  y  values are expressed in screen pixels, not panel width/height pixels. For example, the top-right corner of a panel will be different if the panel is scaled within another panel, window or network viewer. It is better to use  u  and  v , and scale them by the panel Width and Height.
u ,  v  - the position, 0 to 1 in the horizontal and vertical directions
downu ,  downv  - the position, 0 to 1 in the horizontal and vertical directions when the touch first occured (ie. initial touch down location).
contactx ,  contacty  - the width of the contact area.
contactu ,  contactv  - the height of the contact area.
monitor  - monitor number, starting with 0
clicktime  - like  downf , in seconds
elapsedtime  - the number of seconds that finger has been down.
changedtime  - the time since the finger press that the most recent u or v value changed.
dclick  - double-tap occurred
aux  - user supplied data via the  PanelCOMP_Class  method  interactTouch() .  When the event is triggered by the mouse via the Include Mouse option,  aux  will include the mouse buttons used ( 1  for left,  2  for middle,  4  for right, can be tested bitwise).
You can use the attached callback  DAT  (named  mtouchin1_callbacks ) to react to multi-touch events. This is suitable for 2D interfaces that do not require a  Render Pick DAT .
See the  Palette:multiTouch  example in the  Palette  under Tools.
See also the  MultiTouch  page.

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Registers event when Active is On.

parameters.label: Output
parameters.name: outputtype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets how the output is displayed in the table.

parameters.label: Raw Events
parameters.name: log
parameters.description: Events are added to the table in a first in - first out (FIFO) order.

parameters.label: ID Table
parameters.name: changes
parameters.description: Events are processed using one-row-per-finger in the table.

parameters.label: Panel
parameters.name: panel
parameters.description: The  Panel Component  to capture the touch events from.

parameters.label: Relative IDs
parameters.name: relativeid
parameters.description: Reorder the touch ids so only the ones within the specified panel are counted.

parameters.label: Relative Position
parameters.name: relativepos
parameters.description: Output position and normalized coordinates relative to lower left corner of the specified panel.

parameters.label: Occlude Panels by  Hierarchy
parameters.name: occlusion
parameters.description: Only children of the specified panel will receive multitouch events. Touches on parent and sibling panels are ignored.

parameters.label: Occlude Panels by Depth Layer
parameters.name: occbydepth
parameters.description: Enable filtering out multitouch events by Panel Depth Layer.

parameters.label: Occlude Panels Above Depth
parameters.name: occdepthlayer
parameters.description: Multitouch events from panels with a Depth Layer larger than this value will be ignored.

parameters.label: Include Mouse
parameters.name: mouse
parameters.description: When on, the mouse add a touch event when clicked. This event always shares ID 1 with the first touch. Using mouse and multitouch at the same time may result in unexpected behaviours.

parameters.label: Position Threshold
parameters.name: posthresh
parameters.description: A new message will not be added if a finger has moved less than this number of units. The units are determined by the input device, not necessarily the resolution of the screen that it is associated with.

parameters.label: Contact Threshold
parameters.name: contactthresh
parameters.description: Some touch devices have a width and height of a press, representing pressure of amount of finger contact. This is a minimum threshold below which no events are recognized.

parameters.label: Min Rows Displayed
parameters.name: minrows
parameters.description: The minimum number of rows always displayed in the table.

parameters.label: Double Click (secs)
parameters.name: doubleclickthresh
parameters.description: The maximum time allowed between clicks to be registered as a 'double-click'.

parameters.label: Callbacks  DAT
parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: Path  to a  DAT  containing callbacks.

parameters.label: Execute from
parameters.name: executeloc
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines the location the script is run from.

parameters.label: Current  Node
parameters.name: current
parameters.description: The script is executed from the current node location (for example, where 'cc' points to).

parameters.label: Callbacks  DAT
parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: The script is executed from the location of the Callbacks  DAT  specified above.

parameters.label: Specified  Operator
parameters.name: op
parameters.description: The script is executed from the component specified in the   Component   parameter below.

parameters.label: From  Operator
parameters.name: fromop
parameters.description: The path that the script will be executed from if the  Execute From  parameter is set to  Specified  Operator  .

parameters.label: Clamp Output
parameters.name: clamp
parameters.description: The  DAT  is limited to 100 messages by default but with Clamp Output, this can be set to anything including unlimited.

parameters.label: Maximum Lines
parameters.name: maxlines
parameters.description: Limits the number of messages, older messages are removed from the list first.

parameters.label: Clear Output
parameters.name: clear
parameters.description: Deletes all lines except the heading. To clear with a script command, here is an example:  opparm -c /serial1 clear
